desc:
Each pair [x, y] in pairs says that the values x and y are similar. Similarity is symmetric and transitive: if x ~ y and y ~ z then x ~ z. Every value is similar to itself, and values never mentioned in pairs are similar only to themselves.

Two sequences are similar if they have the same length and a[i] is similar to b[i] for every position i. Return true if a and b are similar sequences, otherwise false.

a = [1,2,3], b = [4,5,3], pairs = [[1,6],[6,4],[2,5]]   -> true   (1~6~4, 2~5, 3=3)
a = [1,2,3], b = [4,5,9], pairs = [[1,6],[6,4],[2,5]]   -> false  (3 and 9 are unrelated)
a = [1,2],   b = [1],     pairs = []                    -> false  (different lengths)
hints: If the lengths differ the answer is immediately false. Otherwise the problem is about which values are similar.
Because similarity is transitive, the values split into groups: all values linked by chains of pairs belong together.
Union the two values of every pair (values can be dictionary keys), then compare find(a[i]) with find(b[i]) for every position.
editorial: First compare the lengths. Then build equivalence classes of values with union-find keyed by value (a dictionary instead of an array, because values can be as large as 109). Union x and y for each pair. Two values are similar exactly when they have the same root, or are equal (values never seen get their own singleton class on demand).

Finally check a[i] == b[i] or find(a[i]) == find(b[i]) for each index. Time O((n + m) α), space proportional to the number of distinct values. A DFS per query would be much slower, since a single group may have thousands of values.
